neither: not either of two people or things
used before the first of two negative alternatives
Neither the book nor the film is available.
converge: to tend toward the same point or limit
to come together from different directions
The roads converge near the station.
approach: to get nearer to a value or a place
As n approaches infinity, the error decreases.
a way of dealing with a problem
Both approaches give the same answer.
to move closer to someone or something
odd: not divisible by two without a remainder
break the ice: to ease tension or start a conversation
She broke the ice at the first meeting.
mean: the sum of values divided by their count
range: the span between limits or a set of possible values
The store offers a wide range.
degree: a measure of angle, temperature, or extent
a qualification awarded by a university
derive: to obtain a result from an existing fact or rule
We derive the formula from this identity.
assume: to take something as true for an argument
sequence: an ordered list of terms or events
bound: a limit on the size or value of something
headed for a place or constrained by an obligation
The train is bound for Astana.
eventually: в конце концов; начиная с некоторого момента
after some time or from some point onward
respectively: in the same order as the items already mentioned
Their scores were ten and twelve, respectively.
provided: The command works provided the file exists.
issue: a subject of concern or a problem
We found an issue in the importer.
run: to cause a program or process to execute
process: a running instance of a program, or a series of actions
The operating system schedules each process.
thread: a unit of execution, a chain of messages, or a thin strand
shell: a command interpreter or a hard outer covering
memory: storage for data in a computer, or the ability to remember
allocate: to assign memory or another resource to a task
access: permission or ability to reach or use something
to retrieve or use data or a resource
permission: approval or a right to perform an operation
fault: an abnormal event, a defect, or responsibility for a mistake
A write to a read-only mapping may trigger a page fault.
cache: fast storage holding reusable data or results
load: to bring data into memory or put a burden on something
the amount of work or weight imposed on something
The server is under heavy load.
match: to correspond to or be equal to something
a sporting contest or a correspondence
The first search returned a match.
table: organized rows and columns or a piece of furniture
Store each value in a table.
proof: reasoning or evidence establishing a claim
proof of concept: a small prototype testing whether an idea is viable
The demo is a proof of concept.
edge case: a situation at or near the limits of expected behavior
Test the empty input as an edge case.
carry out: to perform or complete an action
figure out: She figured out why it failed.
look up: to search for information in a reference
Look up an expression in a dictionary.
take into account: to consider something when making a decision
Take the file size into account.
at least: not less than a stated amount
although: introduces a fact contrasting with another
Although the examples differ, the rule is the same.
therefore: as a result of the fact just given
The input is empty; therefore no rows are returned.
